title: Operate the Telete source workflow queue
summary: Submit committed source with a frozen project workflow for checks and selected delivery stages, or use Cell native validation, signed preparation, and deployment.
use_when: Check an exact commit in another repository with a separate project queue, caller-supplied workflow, and selected optional stages.
Operate an explicitly initialized Telete installation.
Configure the shared external work volume or explicitly create or select the shared Cell signing identity through Rust host setup.
do_not_use_when: Infer product health from CI completion.
outcome: Telete retains the exact selected source workflow outcome and its separate acceptance and deployment observations, or records the selected host configuration.
effects: Creates private Git candidates and conditionally advances the selected accepted ref: refs/telete/project-accepted for project workflows or refs/telete/accepted for Cell.
Runs frozen project check and selected trusted preparation and deployment commands; Cell stages add native signing and product deployment instructions.
Explicit storage and signing commands publish shared current-user Cell host settings; initial signing imports one certificate and private key and adds user code-signing trust.

Guarded cancellation retains the original blocked Cell validation operation in an abandonment record before clearing unresolved intent and setting the job phase to cancelled. The failure, process identities, receipts, and queue pause remain retained; cancellation starts no new invocation.
authority: Telete records and runtime correlation checks decide source acceptance.

The caller selects the frozen project workflow. Candidate source supplies its relative check executable; trusted host paths select preparation and deployment. Generic stage success requires the exact retained command completion; commands own stronger domain claims.
Each provider and product retains its own documentation, recognition, installation, and domain authority.
Telete owns the shared current-user storage and signing selectors; Keychain retains private-key authority.
success: The retained job reaches its terminal outcome with all required operations settled.
Host setup publishes the validated requested selection; signing preflight proves key usability at that observation only.
failure_and_recovery: Uncertain admitted effects remain retained and block admission until their exact operation is reconciled.

Service stop also permits a paused blocked deployment with an exact successful receipt, unchanged accepted source, and exclusive settled compiler and deployment resources; the job remains retained for explicit recovery without deployment replay.

Service stop permits one paused Cell queue with a blocked unaccepted failed preparation, an exact unresolved production-generation/candidate/owned-path operation, no final receipt, unchanged accepted base and private candidate, a clean same-repository worktree, and exclusive settled compiler and deployment resources. Other queued, unresolved, preparation, acceptance, or deployment work is absent. Stop preserves all job records and performs no replay; use guarded acknowledge-preparation, correct the failure, and submit a new request. Project workflows are excluded. Jobs with frozen command policy also require the exact outer preparation request and correlated ordinary failed terminal completion under commands/production-N, without timeout, signal, start error, or output-capture error. Missing outer completion and present, dangling, or inaccessible final receipt or active deployment records block stop. Legacy jobs without the outer command retain their existing evidence requirements.
Service stop permits one paused blocked validation with exact completed Autofix evidence and settled resources; it preserves the unresolved job for explicit recovery without validator replay.

A different storage selection is refused. Failed signing preflight preserves existing policy; interrupted certificate creation can leave Keychain effects without a policy and requires explicit inspection and selection.

Cancellation may abandon one paused blocked unaccepted Cell checking job without an aggregate report after either an exact terminal timed-out bounded legacy dispatcher or an exact failed candidate-validator bootstrap with a normal nonzero exit and no timeout, signal, start error, or output-capture error. The bootstrap path requires no dispatcher admission in any supported identity family. Both paths retain all guards: terminal settled children, exclusive resources, unchanged accepted base and exact private candidate, a clean worktree, and no other queued work, preparation, source acceptance, or deployment. Project workflow jobs are excluded. Cancellation starts no invocation, replays no validation, and claims no pass.

Only explicit new project initialization can create local state. Missing, foreign, incomplete, corrupt or mismatched journals do not imply local mode. Worker subprocesses reopen the same retained workspace binding. No relocation or new recovery workflow is supplied.
privacy: Source, workflow parameters, command environments, outputs, diagnostics, and receipts remain private operational records.
Signing policy retains only the public fingerprint, Keychain path, profile and namespace. Private external generation files are removed on ordinary completion; Keychain retains the key.
does_not_authorize: Remote Git publication, automatic product recovery, unrelated credential changes, or implicit product-health claims.

consumers.statement: Current-user operators may use the Telete command interface.

preconditions.statement: New local project queues require explicit --state and init --project, a private normalized local directory, an initialized queue, and supported macOS tools. Cell and existing queues without a local workspace binding retain configured external APFS storage. Check execution uses the macOS filesystem sandbox; Linux execution is not supplied.

Project workflows require a separate project queue; use the same --state directory for every command. Cell submissions require a Cell queue. Cross-mode submissions are rejected. New local queues derive worktrees, temporary files, Cargo downloads, targets and caches from their selected state root; existing queues retain their prior layout.

Initial storage selection requires a mounted external writable APFS volume with ownership enabled. Signing requires configured storage, usable current-user Keychain access, paused drained Telete work, a stopped selected worker, and settled release publication, Telete recovery, and retained legacy manual deployment effects.

inputs.statement: Exact committed source and frozen job policy. A project workflow is read from an absolute regular JSON file and contains a required check command, optional integrate and accept selections, optional trusted prepare and deploy commands, and parameters. Cell jobs retain selected product declarations and optional settings from an absolute regular JSON file mapping explicitly selected canonical product IDs to objects.

Project commands contain program, optional literal args, optional env overrides, and optional timeout_seconds. Check programs are absolute or normalized relative paths below the exact candidate checkout; prepare and deploy programs are absolute host paths. All commands run in the candidate checkout. integrate and accept default to false; parameters defaults to an empty object. Acceptance requires integration and deployment requires preparation. --workflow conflicts with Cell test, deployment, and settings flags.
Host setup selects an exact volume mount and observed UUID or an exact certificate fingerprint, absolute Keychain path and permanent namespace.

outputs.statement: Retained job, gate, preparation, and deployment records.

Shared workspace.json remains schema_version 1 and shared signing.json remains schema 1. Storage status returns configuration path, selection and current root; signing status returns policy, ready and selection source.

data_semantics.statement: Without integration, a project job checks the submitted commit in a clean private checkout even if that commit is already accepted. It requires no accepted ref, Cell inventory or validator build, aggregate Cell report, preparation record, signing selection, or disabled-provider preflight. Exact successful command completion establishes generic check success only.

The fixed order is optional integration, check, optional preparation, optional acceptance, and optional deployment. A stage not selected is not a successful execution. The journal distinguishes submitted source, captured integration base, and tested candidate; merged candidate results do not claim the submitted tree passed unchanged.

CI and Telete are the sole Cell product deployment route. For Cell jobs, an explicit --deploy selection continues through validation and signed preparation for source already in accepted history; without it, accepted source reports already_included. Telete integrates the submitted commit with accepted source and does not restore an older source tree. Explicit deployment does not expand product test selection.
Checking, source acceptance, preparation, instruction completion, and generic command completion have distinct meanings.

For Cell jobs, product selection follows changed owners, explicit prompt and shared platform inputs, and common Telete validation inputs. Shared cell-install and cell-maintenance changes select direct local Cargo consumers. Root Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock changes and other local Cargo dependencies do not expand product selection. Default deployment uses selected products except Telete; an explicit deployment list keeps its exact scope.

For Cell jobs, with tests enabled, selected platform products and new product introductions include shared cell-install tests and, for direct local cell-maintenance consumers, shared maintenance tests. Adding these suites does not select more products.

New Cell jobs freeze the repository-relative check script, host Telete executable path and permitted host environment at submission; executable paths do not freeze host executable bytes. Each bootstrap, check, preparation and deployment resolves its own absolute executable, literal arguments, working directory, complete selected environment, input, timeout and exact context. Candidate validation uses that candidate's regular check script and validator; trusted host commands own preparation and deployment.

Project contexts identify submitted source in source.input, the captured base in source.base (null without integration), and the tested candidate in source.candidate. parameters is the frozen supplied object. outputs.directory is the private absolute job outputs/OPERATION directory. inputs.preparation is null or names the same-candidate successful prepare receipt with stage, candidate, operation, command, result, and stamp; command.context.value.outputs.directory identifies its outputs. Commands own output layout and meaning; Telete supplies no generic package or output schema.
Cell retains deterministic formatting and Clippy autofix. Remaining check and compilation failures stay failed; correct the source and submit a new job.
prompts/repair-instructions.txt and prompts/repair-prompt.txt retain authored text as plain inactive source assets. No workflow reads or executes them.

identity_and_units.statement: Job and request IDs identify operations; Git object IDs identify source; timeouts use seconds.
Volume UUID and mount path identify storage. Certificate SHA-1 selects the certificate, whose signature uses SHA-256; initial validity is 3650 days with an RSA 3072-bit key.

Telete retains program archives with opaque release identities. Its regular runtime executable stays at Telete/install/runtime/bin/telete across install and update; the public command and service use that same file.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Receipts describe the recorded selected scope and exact candidate; CLI status reads retained observations.

access.statement: The supported interface is a local CLI; there is no public Rust CI client or status-snapshot probe.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Initialization without a baseline selects project mode. init --project --accepted-baseline COMMIT selects project mode with a project accepted baseline. A baseline without --project selects Cell mode. Reinitialization cannot replace the repository, mode, or baseline.

Submission freezes the complete project workflow, command selections, parameters, and provider choices. A changed selection requires a new request ID. Reusing an existing request ID returns the original job. Check environment overrides cannot replace Telete context or controlled runtime directories.

Project integration captures refs/telete/project-accepted when the worker claims the job. Candidate merges retain that base. Selected project acceptance uses an expected-old update of that ref; a ref conflict does not select a new base inside that job. Disabled acceptance performs no ref advancement. Cell retains refs/telete/accepted and its native acceptance rules.

Product settings remain frozen in the submission and deployment request. Each installer receives its own settings and selected dependency settings unchanged. Changed settings require a new submission request ID; later input file changes do not change an admitted job. Empty settings preserve product defaults and saved configuration.
One delivery job is active; effect intent is retained before execution and recovery preserves exact identities.

Resolved commands and context contents are retained before execution. TELETE_CONTEXT names the private user-owned regular JSON context file, which must match the retained value before launch. Commands with context clear inherited environment and use the retained environment. Recovery consumes the saved command; identity reuse requires equality including context, environment and timeout. An admitted command without terminal evidence remains unresolved and cannot be replayed automatically.

For Cell validation, process completion and a correlated aggregate report are both required for validation. Preparation's existing record identifies its staged-output handoff. Deployment instruction receipts remain authoritative when the outer command subsequently fails; recovery preserves completed effects without instruction replay. Output-collection failures do not erase known terminal process evidence.

A paused service may stop with one blocked deployment only after its exact successful receipt, unchanged accepted source, and exclusive settled compiler and deployment resources are proved. The job and receipts remain unchanged for explicit recovery; installation and signing still require a drained queue.

A paused Cell service may stop with one blocked unaccepted failed preparation only when its unresolved operation matches the current production generation, exact candidate, and owned result path; both final preparation receipts are absent; accepted base and private candidate are unchanged; and the same-repository worktree is clean. Other queued or unresolved jobs, preparation results, source acceptance, and deployment are absent. Existing stop ownership holds exclusive settled compiler and deployment resources. Stop changes no job, operation, outcome, or receipt and replays nothing. Guarded acknowledge-preparation and a fresh submission remain separate actions. Project workflows are excluded; installation and signing maintenance still require a drained queue. Jobs with frozen command policy require commands/production-N to retain the exact expected preparation request and correlated terminal ordinary nonzero exit with no timeout, signal, start error, or output-capture error. Missing or abnormal completion blocks stop. Present, dangling, or inaccessible final receipt or active deployment records block stop. Legacy jobs without that outer command retain their existing evidence requirements.

A paused service may stop with one blocked validation only after matching job and canonical Autofix reports, its exact successful unbounded dispatcher, exact retained patch, unchanged accepted base and private candidate, and clean worktree are proved. Preparation, acceptance, deployment, and other queued work are absent. Stop holds exclusive settled compiler and deployment resources and changes no job or receipt; installation and signing still require a drained queue.

Storage publication is create-only and repeating the same valid selection does not rewrite it. Shared signing uses host setup and selected Telete admission, worker and deployment locks plus the retained legacy manual-deployment lock, and checks release publication. Configuration preflights before atomic publication. Keychain and file effects are not one transaction.

Guarded Cell validation abandonment retains the original Operation in validation-N.abandoned.json before clearing unresolved intent and setting the job phase to cancelled. It requires either exact timed-out bounded legacy dispatcher evidence or an exact normal failed bootstrap with no dispatcher admission under any supported identity family, plus all source, queue, and resource guards. It preserves the failed outcome, process identities, receipts, and queue pause; advances no accepted source; starts no invocation; and requires a new request ID for another delivery job. Project workflow jobs cannot use this abandonment.

An admitted generic check, preparation, or deployment without terminal evidence remains unresolved. Recovery reconciles exact retained broker terminal evidence without reconstructing or replaying the command. Telete supplies no generic abandonment or acknowledgement for missing terminal evidence and does not roll back uncertain effects.

operational_limits.statement: One heavy gate and two light gates are admitted; process output streams have a 16 MiB bound.

Host setup does not format or mount volumes, enable ownership, migrate journals, stop services, renew certificates, or automatically recover Keychain effects. Shared signing guards the selected Telete state; the operator must settle other independently configured consumers.

The candidate validator dispatcher and aggregate Cargo metadata, Clippy, test, formatter, tool-build, release and production-build commands have no Telete deadline. Git, provider, signing and individual probes retain their bounds; validation success still requires correlated process completion and an aggregate report. Deployment run instructions have no deadline when the manifest omits timeout_seconds; explicitly supplied positive limits remain enforced.

Project check and preparation commands use the macOS filesystem sandbox. Project deployment is a trusted host command without that confinement. All project commands use the heavy broker gate; deployment also holds the existing deployment lock.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Telete state and receipts use explicitly checked schema versions. Retained jobs and deployment operations without settings remain readable as empty settings. Install the matching Telete before admitting jobs with nonempty settings; older Telete does not read that job option.
Contract 2 narrows product selection and adds shared platform tests. Validation receipts remain schema 1; retained receipts keep their recorded scope without migration or reinterpretation.
No cross-release journal migration window is supplied.
Shared workspace.json and signing.json retain their schema-one host formats. Existing Telete signing overrides retain precedence; configure without --host writes a state-specific policy.

Unbounded dispatcher requests use distinct gate identities. Retained bounded dispatcher requests preserve their recorded deadlines and exact command correlation; a timed-out validation is abandoned only through guarded cancellation.
Contract 7 adds guarded service stop for a blocked completed Autofix without changing journal schemas, settling the job or replaying validation.

Contract 8 removes aggregate Rust validation and production command deadlines. Retained command requests keep their recorded time limits and exact correlation; a different command cannot reuse their gate identity.

Contract 9 removes the implicit deployment run deadline for new admissions while preserving explicit manifest limits. Previously interrupted runs with the implicit limit must be reconciled or acknowledged with their matching executor before replacement. Retained process requests are not migrated and remaining instructions are not resumed.
Retained commands without context preserve their original environment behavior, arguments, time limits and correlation. Recovery does not reconstruct admitted commands from current configuration.

Existing Cell queues, jobs, and commands retain their saved policy and recovery semantics. An omitted configuration project field means Cell mode. Project queues use project true and separate refs/telete/project-accepted history. Project workflows add no version fields or schema versions. Install matching Telete explicitly before using the new workflow interface; a source change does not update the installed command.

An optional initialization-derived workspace path in queue configuration selects local storage only for a project queue and must equal its normalized state root. An absent field preserves legacy external storage, including older project queues. Reinitialization cannot add or change the binding. Journal, receipt and contract versions remain unchanged.
Contract 11 removes model repair, outcome notification, and the runtime prompt-store integration. Project workflows no longer accept repair or notify selections.

reliances.statement: Cell validation: provider checks use Chancery's owned bundle codecs and validator.
Cell validation: membership checks use Usher's repository declaration projection.
Git owns merges, patch application, object storage, and reference updates.
macOS owns filesystem sandboxing, Keychain signing, APFS observations, and launchd execution.
Initial certificate generation and fingerprint extraction use the installed OpenSSL command.
Queue storage and selected Cell preparation use shared host setup and exact native signing policy through Telete storage and signing commands. Generic check-only jobs do not look up signing.
